description: A Retrieval-Augmented Generation backend service utilizing a clean Controller-Service-Repository architecture. Integrates with an external, independently-hosted AI Worker via WebSocket for local LLM/embedding offloading, and falls back to external APIs when the worker is unavailable.

techStack.websocket: ws (Backend acts as WS server for external AI Workers)
techStack.auth: Token-based (random string stored in sessions table)
techStack.streaming: Server-Sent Events (SSE) for chat response streaming

dataFlow.ingestion: Route → Controller (validates req) → DocumentService (orchestrates) → WorkerPool (RPC to external worker for embedding) → ChunkRepository (stores in pgvector)
dataFlow.query: Route → Controller (SSE) → RagService → WorkerPool (embeds query via external worker) → ChunkRepository (vector search) → WorkerPool (streaming RPC for LLM generation → each token sent as SSE event) → Controller (ends SSE stream)
dataFlow.aiRouting: WorkerPool acts as a WebSocket server waiting for external AI Workers to connect. When a task arrives, it sends an RPC command to the active worker. If no worker is connected, it falls back to configured external API keys.

keyDesignDecisions: Client is responsible for extracting text and chunking.
Clean Architecture (Simple): Strict separation between HTTP layer (Controllers), Business Logic (Services), and Data Access (Repositories).
External AI Worker: The actual LLM execution happens via a completely separate project running on a local PC, communicating with this backend over WebSocket.
Raw SQL with pg for vector queries, encapsulated entirely within the Repository layer to keep services database-agnostic.

databaseSchema.notes: Only 'vector' extension is created. gen_random_uuid() is built-in since PG 13, so uuid-ossp is unnecessary.

POST /api/auth/register.description: Register a new user and create session

POST /api/auth/login.description: Login with credentials and create session

POST /api/documents.description: Ingest a document with pre-chunked content
POST /api/documents.body: { title, source_type, metadata, chunks: [{ content, chunk_index, metadata }] }

GET /api/documents.description: List all documents for the user

GET /api/documents/:id.description: Get a document with its chunks

DELETE /api/documents/:id.description: Delete a document and its chunks

GET /api/conversations.description: List all conversations for the user

GET /api/conversations/:id.description: Get a conversation with its messages (optional query params from & to for a 1-based inclusive message range, e.g. ?from=1&to=10 for the first 10)

POST /api/conversations/:id/messages.description: Send a message and get RAG response as SSE stream
POST /api/conversations/:id/messages.response: text/event-stream: { type: 'token', content: string } chunks, then { type: 'done', content: string } or { type: 'error', error: string }

GET /admin/login.description: Render the admin sign-in HTML page

POST /admin/login.description: Validate ADMIN_USERNAME/ADMIN_PASSWORD from .env (timing-safe), set httpOnly cookie, redirect to /admin

GET /admin.description: HTML system report: summary cards, level/category/search/date filters, paginated log table (50/page), query params level, category, search, from, to, page

GET /admin/logout.description: Invalidate the admin session cookie and redirect to /admin/login

src/.index.ts: Entry point — starts Express server and mounts WebSocket server
src/.app.ts: Express app setup, middleware, route mounting

config/.index.ts: Validates and exports environment variables (uses dotenv). FALLBACK_API_KEYS split into array.

db/.migrate.ts: Migration runner script (uses fileURLToPath for ESM compat)

routes/.auth.ts: Maps auth endpoints with zod validation
routes/.documents.ts: Maps document endpoints with zod validation
routes/.conversations.ts: Maps conversation endpoints with zod validation
routes/.admin.ts: Maps admin dashboard endpoints (login page, login POST, dashboard, logout)

controllers/.auth.ts: Parses requests, calls AuthService, sends HTTP responses
controllers/.documents.ts: Handles HTTP layer for document ingestion
controllers/.conversations.ts: Handles HTTP layer for chat interactions (sendMessage sets SSE headers and writes event stream)
controllers/.admin.ts: Renders the admin sign-in page and the HTML system report (summary cards, filters, paginated log table)

logging/.index.ts: log(level, message, meta?, category?) — console JSON output + best-effort fire-and-forget insert into system_logs; never blocks callers

services/.auth.ts: Business logic: bcrypt hashing, uuid token generation
services/.workerPool.ts: WebSocket server + RPC dispatch + OpenAI API fallback
services/.exampleEmbeddings.ts: Generates and stores example embeddings once (checks example_embeddings table first)
services/.documents.ts: Orchestrates chunk embedding via WorkerPool and storage
services/.rag.ts: The RAG pipeline: embed query → vector search → build prompt → LLM call

repositories/.user.ts: Raw SQL: INSERT INTO users, SELECT * FROM users
repositories/.session.ts: Raw SQL: session CRUD (also joins user for auth lookup)
repositories/.chunk.ts: Raw SQL: batch insert chunks with array of embeddings, vector similarity search (<=>)
repositories/.message.ts: Raw SQL: message CRUD (also updates conversation.updated_at)
repositories/.exampleEmbedding.ts: Raw SQL: read/write the single example_embeddings row
repositories/.systemLog.ts: Raw SQL: insert system_logs row + filtered/paginated queries + counts

middleware/.auth.ts: Session token verification via Authorization Bearer header
middleware/.adminAuth.ts: Admin dashboard auth: timing-safe .env credential check, in-memory httpOnly cookie sessions, requireAdmin guard
middleware/.error.ts: Global Express error handler (returns 500); routes 4xx/5xx through the logging system
middleware/.validate.ts: zod schema validation wrapper (returns 400 on failure)

seed/.exampleData.ts: Shared example conversation title + example document chunks (single source of truth)

types/.index.ts: Shared TypeScript interfaces (User, Session, Document, Chunk, Conversation, Message, etc.)

environmentVariables.PORT: <number: The port the Express app runs on (default: 3001)>
environmentVariables.WORKER_AUTH_SECRET: <string: Shared secret expected in WS headers when AI worker connects (default: dev-secret)>
environmentVariables.FALLBACK_API_KEYS: <string: Comma-separated list of external API keys (e.g., OpenAI) — split into array by config>
environmentVariables.FALLBACK_LLM_MODEL: <string: Model identifier for external API fallback (default: gpt-4o-mini)>
environmentVariables.FALLBACK_EMBEDDING_MODEL: <string: Model identifier for external embedding API (default: text-embedding-3-small)>
environmentVariables.TOP_K_CHUNKS: <number: Number of top similar chunks to retrieve (default: 5)>
environmentVariables.VECTOR_DIMENSION: <number: Must match embedding model output, e.g., 768 (default: 768)>
environmentVariables.ADMIN_USERNAME: <string: Username for the /admin dashboard sign-in (default: admin)>
environmentVariables.ADMIN_PASSWORD: <string: Password for the /admin dashboard sign-in (default: changeme — set a strong one in .env)>

deviationLog: Removed 'uuid-ossp' extension from migrations — gen_random_uuid() is built-in in PostgreSQL 13+, no extension needed.
Added TOP_K_CHUNKS environment variable to make top-k configurable at runtime.
Added .env.example and .gitignore files outside src/ for better DX.
switched from import.meta.dirname to fileURLToPath for ESM compatibility across Node.js versions.
FALLBACK_API_KEYS config now splits comma-separated string into an array for safer usage.
POST /api/documents returns { document, chunks } instead of just { document } — the chunks are created during ingestion so they're returned immediately.
SessionRepository.findByToken joins users table to return username alongside session — avoids an extra query in auth middleware.
MessageRepository.createMessage also updates conversation.updated_at automatically.
POST /api/conversations/:id/messages now returns a text/event-stream with SSE events (type: 'token' for each delta, type: 'done' on completion, type: 'error' on failure) instead of a JSON body.

WorkerPool has rpcChatStream method for streaming LLM responses: for WS workers it sends { stream: true } in payload and expects deltas via { id, content, done }, for OpenAI fallback it uses stream: true and parses SSE chunks.
rag.ts has answerQuestionStream which accepts an onToken callback called for each token; the controller writes SSE events inside the callback.

New user registration now seeds an example conversation (titled 'Example conversation', empty messages) plus an example document ('Getting started guide') with 5 embedded chunks — users can immediately ask questions and get answers grounded in the example chunks. Seeding is best-effort: failures are logged and never fail registration.

searchSimilarChunks now accepts a userId and joins chunks to documents, scoping vector search to the authenticated user's documents (previously it searched ALL users' chunks globally). rag.ts looks up the conversation to get its user_id.

Example chunks are no longer embedded at registration time: src/seed/exampleData.ts is the single source of truth for example content. src/services/exampleEmbeddings.ts generates the vectors exactly once and stores them in the new example_embeddings table (migration 009): it is triggered on server startup and whenever a worker connects to the WorkerPool (via workerPool.onWorkerConnected), and skips generation if a row already exists. seedExample.ts reuses the stored row; if it is missing or its dimension mismatches VECTOR_DIMENSION it falls back to live embedding.
example_embeddings table: single-row JSONB store of the example embeddings (dimension, source, model, embeddings) — preferred over file-system storage so no extra file or generation script is needed.

Chunks now support an optional heading column (migration 010): client may send heading alongside content in POST /api/documents; rag.ts prepends the heading to the chunk content when building prompt context.

Authorization scoping fix: all by-id lookups now filter on user_id at the repository level. findConversationById/findDocumentById (GET), updateConversationTitle (PATCH), deleteConversationById/deleteDocumentById (DELETE) all take a userId, and rag.ts answerQuestion/answerQuestionStream verify conversation ownership before writing messages — closing cross-user read/delete/write leaks.

GET /api/conversations/:id supports an optional history scope via query params from & to (1-based inclusive range, e.g. ?from=1&to=10 = first 10 messages). Validated by validateQuery middleware (both must be present together, to >= from); the response now also includes total message count.

Chat streaming now supports client-initiated abort: when the client drops the SSE connection, the controller (via req 'close' + res.writableEnded + AbortController) stops writing tokens, and the abort signal propagates through rag.answerQuestionStream → workerPool.rpcChatStream. For WS workers the pool sends { type: 'abort', payload: { taskId } } to kill the LLM generation; for the OpenAI fallback it aborts the fetch with AbortController. The partial answer is NOT persisted on abort.

answerQuestionStream now persists the incomplete streamed answer: tokens are accumulated locally and if the stream ends with an error or abort (rpcChatStream rejects), the partial content is stored as a single assistant message before the error is rethrown. If no token arrived before the failure, nothing extra is persisted. Success path unchanged.

Added a logging system with an admin dashboard (migration 015, system_logs table). src/logging/index.ts exposes log(level, message, meta?, category?) which writes JSON to console AND persists a best-effort, fire-and-forget row to system_logs (level, category, message, user_id, username, meta JSONB); DB failures never block callers. Admin dashboard at /admin: sign-in page (GET/POST /admin/login) with credentials from ADMIN_USERNAME/ADMIN_PASSWORD env vars (timing-safe sha256 compare, httpOnly cookie session in-memory for 24h), /admin renders an HTML report with summary cards (totals, errors 24h, per-level counts), filters (level, category, search, from/to), pagination (50/page), and a log table; /admin/logout invalidates the session. All services are instrumented: auth (register/login/logout success + failure), documents (ingest success/failure, delete), conversations (create/delete, stream started/failed), worker pool (connect/disconnect/errors), server lifecycle, and the error handler now routes 4xx/5xx through the same logger (category 'http') with user context when available. Failed admin sign-ins are logged under category 'admin'.

Message windows fix (post-interruption cleanup): findMessagesWithTotal now orders ASC (chronological, offset counted from the start of history) to correctly satisfy from/to 1-based range queries, and the default 'latest 100 messages' case is served by the new findLatestMessagesWithTotal (DESC + reverse + window total).

SSE failure events no longer leak the raw worker/fallback error into the stream: non-ApiError failures send the generic { type: 'error', error: 'Streaming failed' } event and the real detail is only logged server-side (category 'conversations').

Test env hermeticity: src/config now skips dotenv (skips .env) when NODE_ENV=test so the developer's real .env (admin credentials, WORKER_AUTH_SECRET, FALLBACK_API_KEYS) can never leak into the test suite; tests get values exclusively from tests/setup.ts + defaults.
Restored .env.example (project file listed in projectStructure.filesOutsideSrc) with placeholder values matching the documented environment variables; the real .env remains gitignored.

externalDependencies.aiWorker: A completely separate Node.js project (not tracked in this repo) that runs on a local PC, runs Ollama locally, connects to this backend's WebSocket server using WORKER_AUTH_SECRET, and waits to process embedding/chat generation tasks. Expected WS message format: { id, type: 'embed'|'chat', payload }. Expected response: { id, success, data?, error? }. Aborts: the backend sends { id, type: 'abort', payload: { taskId } } to cancel an in-flight streaming chat; the worker should stop the local LLM generation for taskId and send nothing in return.
